historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Glucocorticoids

starting.description: Adrenal-insufficiency physiology and the effects of adrenal extracts initiated cortical-hormone investigation. Separately, remission of rheumatoid arthritis during jaundice, pregnancy and some vaccine reactions led Hench to seek a protective substance. A reported protective effect of adrenal compound E against animal vaccine reactions helped motivate a planned arthritis test. This hypothesis did not prove that compound E caused the naturally observed remissions, and arthritis benefit of crude adrenal extract had not been established.

inspiration.description: Adrenal insufficiency and extract effects, clinical remission during jaundice, pregnancy or vaccine reactions, and a hormone isolated from adrenal cortex supplied related biological and clinical leads.

steps.description: Adrenal-cortex extracts produced beneficial effects in adrenal insufficiency; researchers isolated and studied individual adrenal steroids, including compound E.

Hench's observed remissions and hypothesis of substance X, together with Kendall's animal observation on compound E and vaccine reactions, prompted a planned trial of compound E after synthesis made it available.

Researchers modified the working adrenal hormones to alter steroid activity, producing prednisolone and prednisone and, with further substitutions, triamcinolone; hydrocortisone also became available for topical use.

Researchers extended established topical steroid effects to inhaled treatment of inflamed airways, reported clinical use of beclomethasone aerosol, and subsequently selected other steroid structures for altered local and systemic activity.

design.description: Researchers prepared and clinically tested compound E, then modified active steroid structures, including ring-A unsaturation and substitutions at carbons 9 and 16, to change pharmacological effects. They formulated steroids for systemic, skin and inhaled administration and later selected structures with different local versus systemic activity. These are substantial chemical, pharmacological and formulation contributions built on working hormone effects, not evidence that the founding class was designed from scratch.

circumstances.description: Hench and Kendall planned the compound E rheumatoid-arthritis test; the breadth of subsequent therapeutic applications surprised many researchers.

limits: Replacement and anti-inflammatory indications have related but distinct biological starting observations.
Cope and Jack directly support selected structural and topical-to-inhaled developments, not a separate origin or detailed synthesis for every later cohort member.
The inhaled-drug evidence describes selected later examples and recollections, not an exhaustive priority history or a guarantee of absence of systemic adverse effects.
conflicts: Hench's hypothesis that an adrenal hormone was the unknown antirheumatic substance remains a hypothesis in his account, not proof that cortisone caused the naturally observed remissions. Kendall says no adrenal-extract benefit in rheumatoid arthritis had been established, consistent with Hench's report of an unimpressive crude-extract test.

Jack calls the first Edinburgh inhaler results equivocal; Morrow Brown recalls an ineffective trial and adrenal suppression at larger doses. These retrospective descriptions differ in emphasis and do not establish universal safety.
gaps: Original adrenal-extract studies and the 1949 Mayo clinical report were not read. The June 1949 Annals reprint was located by PMID and DOI but full text was inaccessible through attempted publisher, PMC and Europe PMC routes.
The 1972 Brown inhaled-beclomethasone report was read only in abstract; its complete methods and results were not read.
Detailed development histories of individual later analogues and priority for every inhaled corticosteroid are outside this class-level collection.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Rheumatoid arthritis remissions during jaundice and pregnancy helped motivate Hench's search for a transferable anti-rheumatic factor.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: The proposed explanatory factor was not thereby proven; animal and chemical work also contributed.
